meta.title: NOSTALGIA Map v2 - water (lakes, Musi, tanks)
meta.format: coordinates [lat, lon] WGS84 (5 decimals); polygons are closed rings (first point repeated); holes = islands
meta.frame: A1 frame lon 78.335-78.561 E, lat 17.312-17.475 N; water bodies intersecting it are listed

confidence_rules.medium: from data but identity or era inferred

attribution: Map reference: DataMeet Municipal Spatial Data (CC BY 4.0) and (c) OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)

Water geometry: (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0, via Overture Maps Foundation base/water release 2026-09-23.0; cross-checked with the OSM-derived Lakeer hyderabad-open-gis-data Waterbodies layer
meta.era_note: Lake outlines are 2026 OSM. Most tanks existed in 2003 (many were larger then: encroachment since has shrunk small kuntas); a few small ponds in new layouts may be post-2003.

lakes.name: Himayat Sagar
lakes.source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overture Maps Foundation base/water, release 2026-09-23.0 (OSM r5411363); simplified to <= 90 vertices
lakes.note: reservoir (1927) on the Esi; mostly south-west of the frame - only its north-east arm reaches the 12000x9000 frame.

lakes.name: Hussain Sagar
lakes.source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overture Maps Foundation base/water, release 2026-09-23.0 (OSM r2833155); simplified to <= 220 vertices
lakes.note: Qutb Shahi-era (1562) lake between Hyderabad and Secunderabad; Tank Bund on the east, Necklace Road on the west/north. Today's OSM shoreline; the west and south shores were reshaped in the 1990s (Necklace Road, Lumbini Park 1994, NTR Gardens c. 2000) so it matches 2003 well; later lake-front works (2010s) changed only small edges.

islands.name: Gibraltar Rock (Buddha statue island)
islands.source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overture Maps Foundation base/water, release 2026-09-23.0 (hole in OSM relation 2833155)
islands.note: the 18 m monolithic Buddha (installed 1992 after sinking in 1990) stands on this rock; reached by boat from Lumbini Park / Eat Street side

lakes.name: Mir Alam Tank
lakes.source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overture Maps Foundation base/water, release 2026-09-23.0 (OSM r39024); simplified to <= 90 vertices
lakes.note: 1806 tank with the multi-arched masonry dam, next to the Nehru Zoological Park (zoo on its east/north-east shore).

lakes.name: Durgam Cheruvu
lakes.source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overture Maps Foundation base/water, release 2026-09-23.0 (OSM w28131043); simplified to <= 90 vertices
lakes.note: "Secret Lake" in a rocky valley between Jubilee Hills and Madhapur; the cable bridge across it is 2020 (absent in 2003).

rivers.name: Musi River
rivers.centreline_note: flows west to east: enters the frame below Langar Houz / Bapu Ghat (Esi confluence), passes Puranapul, the Old City bridges, Chaderghat, Amberpet, Nagole

width_m.riverbed_basis: median bank-to-bank width of the OSM riverbank polygons at 1 km samples between Puranapul and Moosarambagh (data)
width_m.channel_basis: estimate (low confidence): in the dry season of the early 2000s the Musi was a narrow, sewage-fed channel winding through the sandy, weedy bed; it filled the bed only in floods

rivers.note: Riverbed = OSM riverbank areas today; the 2003 bed between the Old City bridges was similar (embanked since the 1908 flood), wider and sandier east of Chaderghat. The banks east of Afzalgunj had dhobi ghats and open riverbed grounds.

rivers.note: tributary from Himayat Sagar joining the Musi near Bapu Ghat / Langar Houz; width estimated (low)
